page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 24 vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core.

This instance is Premium Storage capable and comes bundled with 17279 GB of local storage. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX-512 VNNI and AVX-512 BF16), AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, FMA, and SVM virtualization. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3078.37 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2083.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a PassMark CPU score of 37615.86 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 15915.0. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 73.69 GB/sec for large block reads and 56.07 GB/sec for large block writes. In LLM inference, the server achieves top-tier performance for text generation using a small 135M model at 338.79 tokens/sec, but drops to a weak 6.52 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a large 70B model.

Given the high density of both RAM and local storage, the L24aos_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring large local datasets and substantial memory footprints without the overhead of external storage attachments. It is well-suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, memory-intensive analytics, and local file processing. The lack of GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, though it can handle light, small-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized virtual machine from the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 24 vCPUs (12 physical cores) clocked at 3.7 GHz, 192.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 17279 GB of local storage. The server exhibits strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on Geekbench and stress-ng benchmarks, alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. It also achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 338.79 tokens/sec on small 135M LLM models, though performance drops significantly on larger models. With its high storage-to-vCPU and memory-to-vCPU ratios, the L24aos_v4 provides a cost-efficient profile for data-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive analytics, and data warehousing applications that benefit from massive local storage.
